title: Thy Love Hath Sweetened Me
description: Thy Love Hath Sweetened Me in Tonic Solfa to ST. BRIDE, doh is Bb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: John Brownlie translated these words from the Greek service books for Hymns from the Greek Office Books (Paisley, 1904).
The book printed the words without tunes. They are in Short Metre (6.6.8.6), and this page sets them to ST. BRIDE; any other Short Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Thy love hath sweet-ened me, Thy love, O Christ, di-vine, And by Thy fa-vour Thou hast changed This wil-ful heart of mine.

lines: And by Thy favour Thou hast changed
And in my heart a love instil,
For ever, O Thou Blessed One,
And love and joy shall be
My strength while here I stay;
And love, the spring of all my joy,

source: John Brownlie, Hymns from the Greek Office Books (1904)
licence: Public domain: John Brownlie died in 1925.
credits: Translated by John Brownlie (1857–1925) from the Greek, public domain, as printed in Hymns from the Greek Office Books; set to ST. BRIDE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
